evals.prompt: Brief from Head of Design: the check-in wireframes are approved. Here is a summary of the approved wireframe decisions: the check-in is presented as a full-screen surface (not a sheet) entered from a nav tab or notification. The text input is the dominant element — large, centred, above the fold. Minimal header chrome (back/close icon only). Basil's reply appears below the user's submitted text on the same screen. Error state: inline banner below the input. Crisis state: full-screen card replaces the reply. Produce final visual designs in Figma covering all screens and states.
evals.expected_output: Must cite MD3 documentation URLs for every component used — at minimum: TextField (filled or outlined variant), surface colour roles, typography scale. Must cite HIG for iOS-specific visual decisions. Must create Figma frames using the Figma MCP integration — not describe designs in text only. Frame names must follow the convention: CheckIn / Prompt / Default, CheckIn / Prompt / Typing, CheckIn / Prompt / Submitting, CheckIn / Basil Reply / Default, CheckIn / Error / Network, CheckIn / Crisis / Emergency Card, CheckIn / Crisis / Mental Health Card. Android frames at 360dp width; iOS frames at 390pt width. All text must use named type styles — no one-off font sizes. All colour must use tokens — no hardcoded hex values in frames. All frames must use auto-layout. The visual language must feel calm and warm — not clinical, not chat-app generic. If the brand document does not yet contain Basil visual tokens, the UI Designer must create them and add them to the brand document as part of this pass. Must flag all copy as [COPY: description] — check-in prompt text, Basil reply, error message, crisis card text. Must flag any new design tokens or components introduced. Must NOT change the layout structure or information hierarchy defined in the wireframes. Must hand back to Head of Design with a written summary — not present directly to Gavin.

evals.prompt: Brief from Head of Design: the onboarding wireframes are approved. Here is a summary: five conversation-state screens — Welcome (Basil message, no input yet), Name collection (chat-style input), Context collection (chat-style input), First check-in (full check-in input surface, matches check-in feature design), Basil first reply — plus a sixth fallback state (API unavailable). All screens use a chat-style layout. No form fields anywhere. Produce final visual designs in Figma.
evals.expected_output: Must cite MD3 and HIG for chat-style bubble components, input fields, and safe area handling. Must create frames in Figma using the MCP. Frame names must follow: Onboarding / Welcome / Default, Onboarding / Name / Input, Onboarding / Context / Input, Onboarding / FirstCheckIn / Default, Onboarding / FirstCheckIn / Typing, Onboarding / BasilReply / Default, Onboarding / Fallback / APIUnavailable. Must use the same design tokens established in the check-in design pass — onboarding and the main app must feel visually continuous. Must flag all copy as [COPY: description]. Must ensure the chat bubbles and input style in onboarding are visually consistent with the check-in feature — the user transitions from onboarding into the check-in, and the design must make that feel seamless. Must flag if there are any visual inconsistencies between onboarding and the check-in surface. Must NOT vary from the wireframe structure. Must NOT design a 'skip' button or any exit path from onboarding — the spec explicitly excludes this in v1.
